name: figma-frame-export-lower-third
story: A designer drew a 1920x1080 lower-third frame with a charcoal panel, an amber rule and three named text layers, selected the frame and hit Export > SVG with 'Include id attribute' on and 'Outline text' off.
idioms: no <?xml?> prolog - Figma emits the <svg> element first
root attribute order width, height, viewBox, fill="none", xmlns
zero indentation: every element flush at column 0, one per line
frame contents wrapped in <g clip-path="url(#clip0_12_84)"> with the matching <defs><clipPath id="clip0_12_84"><rect width height fill="white"/>
group and shape ids are the literal Figma layer names, spaces and all (id="Panel bg", id="Lower Third")
uppercase hex fills (#0D1017, #F6A623) and the keyword fill="white" for pure white
fill-opacity="0.92" rather than opacity for a layer alpha
<text> carries the fills and font attributes, xml:space="preserve" AND style="white-space: pre", plus letter-spacing in em
family names not PostScript names (font-family="Archivo" font-weight="bold")
one nested <tspan x= y=> per line, with Figma's fractional baselines (y="838.727")
clipPath <rect> written with width/height only, no x/y, because it sits at the origin
whyThisMatters: This is the single most common file the import will ever be handed, and it would catch an importer that reads text off the <text> node instead of the nested <tspan>, that mistakes the clipPath's <rect> for the growable panel, or that drops the id-as-layer-name labels because of the space in 'Panel bg'.
